title: Reproductive Rights and Abortion Access
question_text: What legal framework should govern abortion access?

stances.text: ensure abortion is legal, accessible, and publicly funded at all stages of pregnancy.
keep abortion legal and accessible through the second trimester with rare exceptions afterward.
allow abortion in the first trimester and in cases of rape, incest, or maternal health risks.
restrict abortion to only cases involving rape, incest, or serious threats to the mother's life.
ban abortion completely with no exceptions and impose criminal penalties for providers and patients.

title: Campaign Finance Reform
question_text: What rules should govern money in political campaigns and elections?

stances.text: ban all private money in politics and publicly fund campaigns
strictly limit corporate donations and dark money groups
require full disclosure of all political donations
reduce restrictions on political donations and spending
eliminate all campaign finance laws and limits

title: Childcare Affordability & Access
question_text: How should government address the cost and availability of childcare?

stances.text: Establishing publicly funded universal childcare so that all families have access regardless of income
Significantly expanding subsidies and provider grants to make childcare affordable for low- and middle-income families
Offering targeted tax credits and subsidies for families below a set income threshold while supporting providers through training and facility grants
Reducing regulations on childcare providers to increase supply and lower costs, with limited subsidies reserved for the lowest-income families
Leaving childcare to the private market and families, with no government subsidies or mandates that increase costs for providers and taxpayers

title: City Sanitation and Cleanliness
question_text: How should your community approach street cleanliness and sanitation?

stances.text: Significantly expand sanitation staffing, cleaning frequency, and free community disposal access; treat poor conditions as a services failure
Increase sanitation crews and prioritize historically underserved neighborhoods to equalize cleanliness communitywide
Maintain current sanitation services while enforcing anti-dumping laws for businesses and large property owners
Rely primarily on enforcement of anti-littering and property maintenance laws; hold residents and businesses responsible
Privatize sanitation services and require residents and businesses to contract for cleanup directly

title: Civil Rights and Social Justice
question_text: What role should government play in addressing racial and social inequality?

stances.text: mandate racial equity requirements in all institutions and provide reparations
strengthen civil rights enforcement and address systemic discrimination
maintain current civil rights laws while promoting equal opportunity
limit federal civil rights enforcement to clear cases of discrimination
eliminate affirmative action and all race-based government programs

title: Climate Change and Environmental Protection
question_text: What priority should climate change receive in energy and economic policy?

stances.text: declare a climate emergency and ban all activities that increase carbon emissions
rapidly transition to renewable energy and phase out fossil fuels by 2030
invest in clean energy while gradually reducing reliance on fossil fuels
let market forces drive any transition to cleaner energy sources
reject climate change policies and focus on economic growth instead

title: Data Center Development & Energy Costs
question_text: How should government manage the growth of large-scale data centers?

stances.text: Imposing a moratorium on new data center construction until energy infrastructure can support demand without raising costs for residential ratepayers
Requiring data centers to fund their own dedicated power generation and barring utilities from passing data center infrastructure costs to residential customers
Allowing data center development with impact assessments, energy cost-sharing agreements, and community benefit requirements before approval
Encouraging data center development through streamlined permitting while requiring transparency about projected energy demand and rate impacts
Welcoming data center investment with competitive incentives and minimal regulatory barriers, trusting that economic growth and tax revenue will benefit all residents

title: Economic Development Incentives
question_text: How should government attract businesses and support economic development?

stances.text: No corporate tax incentives; invest in public services and infrastructure to attract business organically
Small business support and local entrepreneur programs only; avoid large corporate subsidies
Targeted incentives for specific industries with community benefit agreements and job quality requirements
Compete actively for major employers with significant tax abatements and infrastructure investment
Offer maximum incentives to attract any large employer; economic growth is the top priority

title: Fossil Fuel Policy
question_text: What role should fossil fuels play in the nation's energy future?

stances.text: immediately ban all new fossil fuel drilling and extraction
stop issuing new permits for fossil fuel drilling
maintain current levels of fossil fuel production with existing environmental regulations
expand fossil fuel drilling permits
remove environmental restrictions and maximize fossil fuel extraction

title: Growth and Development Pace
question_text: How should government manage population growth and new development?

stances.text: Impose growth limits; require voter approval for major annexations or large-scale developments
Allow growth only where existing infrastructure can support it; slow approvals until capacity catches up
Plan proactively — invest in infrastructure ahead of growth to support responsible expansion
Streamline permitting, reduce fees, and actively recruit development to grow the tax base
Remove regulatory barriers to development entirely; let market demand determine growth pace

title: Criminalization of Homelessness
question_text: How should government address people sleeping or camping in public spaces?

stances.text: Protecting the right to sleep in public spaces and redirecting enforcement budgets toward permanent supportive housing and mental health services
Decriminalizing public sleeping while investing in shelter capacity, outreach workers, and voluntary service connections
Allowing enforcement only when adequate shelter beds are available, with citations diverting people to services rather than the criminal justice system
Prohibiting encampments on public property with graduated warnings and penalties, while requiring jurisdictions to maintain basic shelter options
Banning public camping and sleeping with criminal penalties to maintain public safety and order, relying on existing social services for those who seek help

title: Homelessness Response
question_text: What should be your community's primary strategy for addressing homelessness?

stances.text: Housing-first: provide permanent supportive housing with no preconditions; avoid criminalization entirely
Expand shelter capacity and services as the primary strategy; use enforcement only after services are offered
Invest in outreach, shelter, and mental health services while enforcing reasonable public space rules
Enforce anti-camping ordinances as the primary tool while maintaining basic outreach programs
Prioritize strict enforcement of trespassing and camping bans; minimize public spending on homeless services

title: Affordable Housing
question_text: What role should government play in making sure people can afford housing?

stances.text: Directly build and operate public housing so anyone who needs a home can get one
Use rent caps, require new developments to include affordable units, and publicly fund new housing
Offer targeted help like subsidies for affordable projects, first-time buyer assistance, and easier building permits
Cut regulations and zoning rules so private developers can build more housing
Stay out of housing entirely and let the market decide prices and supply

title: Jail Capacity and Incarceration Alternatives
question_text: How should government respond to jail overcrowding and criminal justice demand?

stances.text: Redirecting incarceration funding into community-based mental health, addiction, housing, and restorative justice programs to shrink the jail system
Reducing the incarcerated population through pretrial diversion, bail reform, and treatment alternatives rather than building new capacity
Upgrading jail facilities only as needed to meet constitutional standards, without expanding overall capacity
Building additional jail capacity to address overcrowding and facility deficiencies
Expanding jail capacity and enforcement as the primary response to crime, prioritizing detention over alternatives

title: Environmental Protection vs. Development
question_text: How should your community balance new development with environmental preservation?

stances.text: Require significant green space, tree preservation, and environmental review before approving any development
Protect existing parks and tree canopy strictly; require developers to fully offset any environmental impact
Apply consistent environmental standards while giving developers reasonable flexibility on implementation
Allow developers to pay fees in lieu of on-site preservation; prioritize economic activity over green space
Remove local environmental restrictions beyond what state and federal law requires

title: Local Immigration Enforcement
question_text: How should your community's law enforcement relate to federal immigration enforcement?

stances.text: Refuse all ICE detainers; prohibit local employees from sharing immigration status information with federal agencies
Comply only with court-ordered detainers; protect undocumented crime victims and witnesses from referral
Follow federal law as required but do not use local resources for proactive immigration enforcement
Honor ICE detainers and share information proactively when federal agencies request it
Direct local police to actively assist with immigration enforcement and support federal detention operations

title: Public Safety Approach
question_text: How should your community fund and operate public safety services?

stances.text: Redirect a significant portion of the police budget to social services, mental health, and community programs
Maintain current police staffing but shift non-violent calls to unarmed mental health co-responders
Keep current public safety funding while adding crisis response teams for mental health and addiction calls
Increase police staffing, equipment, and pay to improve response times and deter crime
Make expanding the police budget the top spending priority over other services

title: Religious Freedom
question_text: What role should religion play in government, public institutions, and policymaking?

stances.text: strictly separate religion from all public institutions and prohibit religious exemptions from civil rights laws.
protect religious freedom while ensuring it doesn't override anti-discrimination protections in employment and housing.
balance protecting religious practices with maintaining equal treatment under the law for all citizens.
protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs.
strongly protect religious freedom and allow religious organizations complete autonomy in their operations and hiring practices.

title: Rent Regulation
question_text: What role should government play in regulating rents and protecting tenants?

stances.text: Expand rent control to all rental units with strong tenant protections and just-cause eviction requirements
Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units
Maintain current tenant protections while allowing market rents for new construction
Limit rent regulations to subsidized units; allow market rents broadly
Oppose rent control entirely; rents should be set by the market without government intervention

title: Residential Zoning
question_text: What should guide decisions about housing density and neighborhood character in your community?

stances.text: Protect existing neighborhood character strictly; require community votes before any rezoning
Allow modest density increases (duplexes, accessory units) with strong design review and neighborhood input
Allow multifamily and mixed-use near commercial corridors while protecting most residential zones
Upzone broadly to allow multifamily by right; streamline approvals and reduce parking requirements
Eliminate single-family-only zoning; allow any housing type on any lot communitywide

title: Transgender Athletes
question_text: How should sports leagues determine eligibility for transgender athletes?

stances.text: allow all transgender athletes to compete on teams matching their gender identity without any restrictions or requirements.
should allow transgender athletes to compete on teams matching their gender identity after completing basic documentation of their transition.
create separate transgender divisions or allow case-by-case decisions based on individual circumstances and sport requirements.
require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth.
completely ban all transgender athletes from competing in any organized sports competitions.

title: Transportation Priorities
question_text: Where should government focus its transportation investment?

stances.text: Prioritize pedestrian infrastructure, cycling networks, and public transit; reduce parking requirements communitywide
Invest equally in roads and multimodal options; require bike lanes and sidewalks on all new road projects
Maintain roads while selectively adding transit connections and pedestrian improvements where density supports it
Focus on road capacity and traffic flow; transportation investment should serve the majority who drive
Prioritize highway access and abundant free parking as the foundation of local transportation policy
